attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, published under his name and endorsed.

semantics.note: 'I would be truly astonished' expresses firm, high-confidence expectation that hallucinations would not reach human expert levels by end-2024. It is not hedged probability, so it is a scored forecast. The normalisation keeps the threshold and the horizon.

contract.note: The support and contradiction conditions fit the words. But the speaker named no task, domain, or metric for 'human expert levels', so any baseline chosen would decide the result. That makes the result interpretation-dependent, despite the contract's flag of false. The contract also cites policy .3 while frozen under .4.

output.rationale: The deadline (2024-12-31) has passed. The packet contains no used evidence item. The two sources considered (FaithBench, MedHalu) do not measure a human-expert error rate on the same tasks as the models. No measurement in the packet compares model and expert hallucination rates, so neither the support nor the contradiction condition can be checked.
